text: dsh-switchman 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的调度与上下文管理插件，通过宿主扩展注册设置、提示上下文和会话工具，并提供独立设置面板。它支持六类模型派发池与意图路由、团队模式、语言偏好、上下文水位提醒和自动整理交接，也附带可发现的技能。适合需要按任务选模型、协作派发或管理长会话的 DSH 用户；模型路由需在设置中配置。

dsh-switchman is a DSH Web plugin for model dispatch and long-session management. It adds a settings panel, six workload-based model pools, intent routing, optional agent teams, context watermarks, automatic trimming and handover, and bundled skills. Configure model routes in its settings.
我想按任务类型给 DSH 子代理分配不同的模型。
能不能在长会话接近上下文上限时自动整理并继续？
我希望 DSH 根据对话意图自动挑选候选模型。
怎么让 DSH 的 agent 团队按共享任务板协作？
How can I route delegated tasks to different models by workload?
I need long DSH sessions to trim old context and resume work automatically.
Can DSH choose a model from my candidates based on the conversation?
How do I enable coordinated agent teams in DSH?
dsh-switchman 的功能「模型派发池」：按经济、机械、主力、困难、视觉和评审任务配置模型候选与排序。每轮提示会给出推荐表，启用强制模式后还会拦截池外的子代理模型调用。
dsh-switchman 的功能「上下文水位与交接」：按会话 token 水位提示收紧读取预算，并在强制水位触发交接文档、压缩和恢复会话；也可用 /ctx-handover 手动发起。
dsh-switchman 的功能「自动上下文整理」：在空闲边界折叠已消费的会话区间，以摘要替换请求视图并保留最近消息；可配置自动、建议或仅测量模式。
dsh-switchman 的功能「意图模型路由」：选择 Auto 模型后，分类器会根据近期对话从候选模型中路由，并在一轮内固定决策；可配置阈值、缓存窗口和备用路由。
dsh-switchman 的功能「Agent Teams 模式」：开启后动态注入团队协作规程并协调启用 DSH 团队能力；可选择将模型派发池同步到子代理授权白名单。

dsh-switchman README · dsh-switchman：> **The switchman family**, same author, same dispatch doctrine: [opencode-switchman](https://github.com/mrzturn/opencode-switchman) (the OpenCode original) · [zcode-switchman](https://github.com/mrzturn/zcode-switchman) (the ZCode port) · **dsh-switchman** (this repo, the DeepSeek Harness edition).

> A water meter on the context; every task finds its own lane.

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：Two pains creep in once you've worked in DSH for a while. First, sessions get heavier the longer they run: history bloats the context into hundreds of thousands of tokens, the model starts forgetting, slowing down, costing more — and a manual /compact loses detail. Second, the main model does everything itself: chasing files, running tests, reconciling data — most of that work belongs on a cheaper model.

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：dsh-switchman is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). Once installed, the main model stops doing and starts dispatching: measure the watermark, pick a lane, hand out tasks, check acceptance. It's not a new model — it's a dispatch doctrine hooked onto DSH plus a settings page, and it does eight things:

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：**1. Context watermark: long sessions don't blow up.** Every turn counts session tokens in real time, and three escalating lines tighten the screws: 80k (soft, adjustable) nudges "time to delegate"; 120k (hard) shrinks the single-read budget and steers toward wrap-up; 150k (force) hands over automatically — writes the handover document (the append-only session log is the full-fidelity backup), compacts the context, wakes the session to continue, task unbroken. Background subagents still running at handover aren't lost either: their ids, tasks, and report paths go into the handover document, so the resumed session knows where to collect reports and never dispatches twice. Every subagent carries its own hard cap and exits after writing its HANDOFF summary. When the automatic intervention doesn't suit you, take over manually: `/ctx-pause` stops all watermark actions (measurement keeps running, the live watermark line switches to paused — it just stops acting), `/ctx-resume` restores them at any time — after a DSH restart the enforcement also comes back on its own, a temporary let-go, not a permanent off; `/ctx-handover` doesn't wait for the water

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：**2. Six dispatch pools: the right model for every job.** Economy (batch small chores), mechanical (template rewrites), main (day-to-day coding), hard (hard reasoning and large refactors), vision (images), review (independent verification). On the settings page you tick candidates, order priorities, grade S/A/B/C, and pin a per-route thinking effort — the effort dropdown lists the levels that model actually supports, not a generic three. Every turn's prompt carries a `[SWITCHMAN:POOLS]` recommendation table, and the main model dispatches by it. Three enforcement modes: off / advice / force (force = out-of-pool models get rejected outright).
dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：**3. Agent Teams mode: from solo to a team.** Off by default — after install it's lightweight subagent dispatch. Two independent toggles on the settings page:

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：- **Agent teams** — once on, the team doctrine is injected (delegate by default + tiered verification + shared task-board discipline) and DSH's Agent Teams is enabled automatically: the main model can pull standing teammates (`spawn_teammate`), put work on a shared task board (`team_task_*`), and message teammates. When to form a team follows clear discipline: parallelizable independent subtasks, bulky self-contained work, high main-context watermark, need for role separation; one-off single-point investigations still go to a subagent. Turn the toggle off and the team clauses vanish without residue, and team tools are never yanked from sessions still running.
- **Subagent model whitelist sync** — DSH keeps an authorization whitelist "allow agents to pick models for subagents": routes chosen in a pool but not authorized get rejected when dispatched by name (marked ⚠ in teams mode). Flip this toggle and the union of all six pools is written into that whitelist wholesale — switchman becomes the single source of truth, no double configuration. The whitelist takes effect as a per-new-session snapshot; the sync only affects sessions started afterwar

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：The session header gives at-a-glance feedback: the ⚡ "autonomous team" badge and ◇ with the session's actual model; while an auto-handover runs, a live indicator shows "handover in progress · writing handover doc / compacting context / waking the successor".

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：**4. Language preferences: ask once, remember forever.** One dropdown each for replies, code comments, and documents; scope is global or per-project (`.switchman/lang.json`). Skipping is fine — on first use you're asked once in your DSH interface language, and every session obeys the answer afterwards.

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：**5. Interface language: the plugin itself speaks your language.** In the "Interface" section atop the settings page sits the "Interface language" dropdown (setting key `uiLocale`): Auto (default, follows the DeepSeek Harness app language), or any built-in interface language picked by hand — options always appear under the language's own endonym, never translated. It switches only the plugin's own interface (badge, home panel, settings page), never the DSH app language: selecting previews live with no restart, the choice is remembered after save and restored on the next launch, and any failure falls back to the app language; the dictionaries ship inline in the plugin bundle, nothing to download.

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：**6. Tiered verification: every change gets checked.** Changes over 20 lines go to a tester; over 300 lines, or touching core / security / data-consistency logic, additionally to an independent reviewer. The review model is picked anchored on the model of "the agent that wrote the diff", avoiding it where possible; when the pool can't, the conclusion declares DOWNGRADED. Say "don't use the team" once and it drops back to solo instantly.

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：**7. `/vision`: text-only models can still handle images.** When the main model can't read images, DSH rejects image-bearing messages at the gate. Paste the image, type `/vision what's wrong with this image`, and the image goes to a vision-pool model; the verdict comes back into the current session. A heads-up "current model can't read images" appears above the input box; when a direct image send is rejected, the message is rewritten as `/vision` and resent automatically — no manual redo; with no vision pool configured the command refuses and points to the settings.

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：**8. Intent routing: the right model picks itself.** A new "Intent Routing" group on the settings page: a master switch (off by default — enabling requires a classifier and at least one candidate), the classifier's small-model route (provider + model + optional effort — TypeSafe Jev-style decision models and general chat models both work, with tolerant output parsing), a classifier type three-way choice (auto / decision / chat), an independent candidate list (each candidate: provider + model + optional effort + a one-line capability note), cache window seconds (default 300, aligned to the ~5-minute prompt caches vendors provide), a switch confidence threshold (default 80), a classification timeout (default 60000 ms), history message count (default 6) and character budget (default 2400), plus an optional fallback model. The model picker gains an "Auto" entry under the "Auto · Switchman" group (the client renders it localized — "Auto (intent routing)" in English); once selected, every user message is classified to pick the best-fitting candidate and the decision is locked for that turn: when confidence is lacking or the cache window is still ope

dsh-switchman README · Why you need it：Worth installing even with a single model — watermark control and tiered verification don't care how many models you have, and long single-model sessions benefit just the same.

dsh-switchman README · Bundled skills：- **db-query** — read-only MySQL / Redis verification: run SQL to reconcile data, inspect cache keys / TTL, cross-database consistency checks; every write refused. Needs one-time initialization before first use (see below).
- **git-commit-message** — generates disciplined commit messages; text only, never runs git for you.
- **requirement-docs** — the house standard for requirement analysis / PRD / design docs; output is archived to `docs/requirements-and-design/`.

dsh-switchman README · Quick start：1. **Install** — have an agent run it in any session, or use the Web plugin management page:

```
   plugin_manager: install_bundle  target=dsh-switchman
   ```

Or install from a local checkout (link mode; after an update, `remove_bundle` + `install_bundle` again):

```
   plugin_manager: install_bundle  target=/path/to/dsh-switchman
   ```

Or with the `dsh` CLI in a terminal — pick the profile matching how you run it:

dsh-switchman README · Quick start：```bash
   dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-switchman      # Web GUI
   dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-switchman   # desktop app
   ```

2. **Restart DSH** — quit the app completely and reopen it (a page refresh doesn't count); only then does the client module table recognize the bundle.

3. **Configure** — Settings → dsh-switchman, or "Switchman Dispatch Center" in the home sidebar. It's a single page of config and looks like this — walk it top to bottom and you're done:

dsh-switchman README · Quick start：- **Interface** — the plugin's own UI language. The dropdown in the shot sits at English — a live preview of switching; the shipped default is Auto (follows the DSH app language). Picking a language flips the whole page on the spot and is remembered after save; switch back to Auto anytime.
   - **Languages** — the languages of agent output. The scope in the shot is "Global (this profile)" (per-project works too, each reading `.switchman/lang.json`); the reply / code comments / documents dropdowns in the shot all sit at English, each displayed as "endonym (tag)" — e.g. "English (en)" — with a "current: …" status line beneath each. Leaving all three unset is fine too: asked once on first use, remembered from then on.
   - **Dispatch pools** — six cards in two rows of three: economy, mechanical, main on top; hard, vision, review below. Tick candidate models grouped by provider; tick "manual order" and a card becomes a numbered priority list reorderable with ↑ ↓ ×; every route can pin a thinking effort (default "follow lane"). The summary line at the top updates live — in the shot: "4/6 pools configured · 2 ranked · mode advice".
   - **Capability ran

dsh-switchman README · Quick start：4. **Verify** — the ⚡ "autonomous team" badge appears in the session header (with ◇ beside it showing the session's current model); or simply ask the model "what's the heading of the last section of your system prompt" — the answer should mention the dsh-switchman doctrine.

**db-query one-time initialization** (script dependencies install inside the skill directory, nothing pollutes your project):

```bash
bash <install-dir>/skills/db-query/scripts/setup.sh
```

dsh-switchman README · Quick start：**Classifier model tips:** to run the decision model locally, serve `tev1:4b-mxfp8` with Ollama — set the classifier kind to the decision endpoint (systemone), fill the endpoint with `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/systemone`, and set the model name to `tev1:4b-mxfp8`. For the chat classifier from the LLM catalog, prefer a small cloud model, or a small local model without thinking (reasoning) — turning thinking off lowers both latency and the classification-timeout failure rate.

dsh-switchman README · Default configuration：Everything below is the full set of defaults after a fresh install (authoritative source: the zod schema in `host/config.js`).

**Interface and languages**: `uiLocale` = `auto` (follows the DSH app language); `langScope` = `global`; `langConversation/Comments/Docs` = empty (asked once in the first session and then remembered; the comment and document languages follow the conversation language).

dsh-switchman README · Default configuration：**Dispatch pools**: all six lanes (economy/mechanical/main/hard/vision/review) start with empty candidates (= the system default models, no intervention); manual ordering and pinned effort are off/empty; `dispatchEnforce` = `advice` (advisory only, nothing enforced).

dsh-switchman README · Default configuration：**Context watermark**: soft `80000` / hard `120000` / force `150000` tokens; single-read budget `3000`; over-budget behavior `cap` (truncate with a warning); `wmAutoHandover` = on (at force, automatic handover: write doc + compact); the subagent hard cap = on (sharing 150k).

**Agent Teams**: `teamsMode` = off; `syncWhitelist` = off (the two toggles are independent of each other).

dsh-switchman README · Default configuration：**Intent routing** (unavailable by default; needs a classifier + at least one candidate + the master switch on): `intentEnabled` = off (while off, the Auto entry stays hidden and sessions already on Auto fall through the fallback chain); the classifier route is unset; the classifier type is `chat`; the candidate list is empty (the preset categories join routing only once given a model); cache window `300` s / switch confidence threshold `80` / classification timeout `60000` ms; history `6` messages / `2400` characters; `intentContextWindow` = `200000`.

dsh-switchman README · Default configuration：**Context trim**: `trimEnabled` = on; `trimMode` = `auto` (fully automatic); growth gate `22500` tokens + increment `50000` tokens; pressure `60%` / emergency `95%`; protected tail `6` messages; fold cadence cap `6` per hour; side model unset (inherits the session model) — details in the "Automatic context trim" section below.

dsh-switchman README · Default configuration：**Out-of-the-box notes**: ① intent routing being unavailable out of the box is by design — three steps to switch it on (classifier, candidates, the master switch); ② Auto's effective window is 200000 out of the box — the guardrail guarantees 0.8×window ≥ force (150000), so the core compaction line (160000) always sits after the smooth-handover line (150000); ③ the most tangible out-of-the-box effect is the watermark trio: 80k nudges delegation / 120k tightens reading / 150k backs up and hands over automatically — no configuration needed.

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：Long sessions stay cheap: consumed conversation ranges are folded into compact deterministic summaries — fully automatically, without breaking the provider prompt cache. At an idle boundary the trim engine (`host/context-trim/`) picks the ranges worth folding, a side model writes the summary (only under emergency pressure does a mechanical fold run instead — no side-model call), and the fold is committed to the session's fold state. From then on every outbound request is rebuilt from that state — summary blocks replace the folded ranges, the live tail stays untouched. The stored session is never rewritten, and nothing ever happens mid-stream.

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：- **`off`** — measure only: usage and cache-hit sampling still runs; no banner, no folds.
- **`advisory`** — the session model folds itself: the `ctx_trim_fold` and `ctx_trim_status` tools plus the protocol head are exposed for it.
- **`auto`** (default) — everything above plus automatic folds at the idle boundary, in three tiers: a growth gate (growth > `trimGrowthTokens` measured from the last fold's post-fold low — the anchor that keeps the gate armed after folds committing at high view points — AND a contiguous compressible increment ≥ `trimIncrementTokens`; the increment floor is what actually binds), a pressure tier (`trimPressurePercent` of the context window), and an emergency tier (`trimEmergencyPercent` — a mechanical fold with its own cooldown). Pressure and emergency usage is measured on `max(view, wire)`, i.e. on the real provider prompt when it is known.

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trimEnabled` | `true` | Master switch. OFF disables folding and metrics entirely (the listener degrades to a pure pass-through). |
| `trimMode` | `auto` | `off` measure only / `advisory` model-driven folds / `auto` system-driven folds. |
| `trimGrowthTokens` | `22500` | Growth gate: fold when the outbound view grew this much since the last fold. |
| `trimIncrementTokens` | `50000` | Gate companion: the contiguous compressible increment must also reach this size. |
| `trimPressurePercent` | `60` | Pressure tier: fold when view usage reaches this percent of the context window. |
| `trimEmergencyPercent` | `95` | Emergency tier: forced mechanical fold (no side-model call) at this percent. |
| `trimWindowTokens` | `0` | Effective-window cap for tier math: tiers are computed against min(model window, cap). `0` = follow `wmForceTokens`. |
| `trimProtectedTail` | `6` | The last N messages are never folded. |
| `trimMaxFoldsPerHour` | `6` | Side-model fold cadence cap per rolling hour (emergency folds are exempt). |
| `trimSideModel` | unset | Route for the summary side model. Empty = inherit t

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：**Trigger paths.** Tier checks run at the idle boundary and, as a fallback for hosts where idle status events are unreachable, after each model-stream completion (throttled to one evaluation per 60 s per session). Every decision — folds and no-ops alike — is appended as one timestamped `key=value` line to `decisions.log` in the trim state directory (see `trimStateDir`), giving folds an offline audit trail; the row vocabulary (`view-applied`, fold decision/outcome rows, `surface-replace`, `surface-replace skipped reason=…`) is catalogued in [docs/context-trim.md](./docs/context-trim.md).

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：**Wire truth and steady state.** Decision rows carry `view=<n>` and, once a response has landed, `wire=<n>` — the real provider prompt (uncached input + cache read + cache write, sampled from the stream's usage event). The view estimate counts the messages array only and always reads smaller than the wire by the fixed overhead (measured ≈ 17.3k: system prompt + tool schemas + persona), so pressure and emergency tiers evaluate on `max(view, wire)`, and only `wire` is a prompt-size reading. On a 150k window the healthy sawtooth runs wire ≈ 40k just after a fold ↔ 88–90k at the next one (≈27%–60% of the window), one fold per ~50k of raw growth, with the ceiling pinned near 90k by the pressure tier rather than by the window. If `view` climbs while no `surface-replace` row ever appears, read the skip rows (`incomplete-seqs`, `no-service`, `compaction-lock`).

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：**Host-compaction epochs.** Fold refs are anchored in message ids and content hashes, so a host-side compaction that replaces the re-send history ages the whole ledger out at once: no block locates, the view silently falls back to raw history (fail-open — the decision log records `view-applied applied=0`), and the plugin re-anchors its growth baseline at the post-compaction view on the next request. The host compaction is thus the backstop trim layer, and plugin folds do the fine-grained work within one host epoch. Some dispatches hand out fully frozen request arrays or option objects (the current agent loop deep-freezes assembled requests); for those `injectView` reports the outcome in the decision log: `nothing-to-apply` (no located fold blocks — raw history IS the view), `in-place`/`swapped` (the fold view shipped), or `none` (a fold existed but the frozen dispatch could not carry it — the wire ships raw history). **Surface replace is the shipping path when available** (`surfaceFold`, default on): at the serial `agent/turn-stopping` boundary plus an idle sweep, the plugin appends the host-style shadow-price metering event and ONE `us

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：**How folds preserve cache hits.** Every fold re-pays the prefix once; the goal is amortized cost, not a perfect hit rate. The engine enforces the cache contract: folds are append-only — the frontier only moves forward and the frozen zone is never edited again; the view is rebuilt deterministically from (history, fold state), so the serialized prefix stays byte-identical between folds and the provider cache keeps hitting; fold boundaries never split an assistant tool-call from its tool result; the last `trimProtectedTail` messages are exempt; and everything fails open — an internal error degrades to a pass-through, never a broken request.

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：**Compaction arbitration.** Two automatic trimmers over one history would double-summarize and destroy each other's frontier, so `cordis.patch.yml` sets `auto: false` on the host's `dsh-compaction-basic` rows: context-trim becomes the single semantic trimmer. Manual `/compact` keeps working, and the force-tier handover (which borrows that same manual path) is untouched. Overflow recovery moves to trim: an over-window attempt fails once, then the emergency tier folds the view so the next attempt fits.

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：**Fork inheritance.** A forked session (a subagent fork) inherits the parent's fold state copy-on-fork — but only when the parent state exists and the child's history actually resolves the parent's frontier; otherwise the child starts clean. One inheritance per child, idempotent across restarts.

dsh-switchman README · Automatic context trim：**The watermark reads the view.** The watermark banner reports the outbound view's token count (what the model actually sees after folding) instead of the stored tally, so a heavily folded session no longer pins the watermark at the hard tier.

dsh-switchman README · How it works：- The host half (`index.js` + `host/`) injects the byte-stable system-prompt sections (language / lanes / watermark protocol / teams) plus the live watermark line through the tail runtime-context snapshot (a channel that appends instead of rewriting the prompt head, so the provider prompt cache stays intact), the read-budget plus enforce double gate, and four slash commands (the ctx trio + `/vision`). A saved setting takes effect at the very next prompt assembly — no restart.
- The client half (`client.js`) renders the settings page, the ⚡ badge and ◇ model marker in the session header, and the live handover indicator; config snapshots are read and written through the Host route family.
- The "Switchman Dispatch Center" entry in the home sidebar opens that same settings page as a center panel in one click; the original settings entry stays.
- `cordis.patch.yml` keeps the factory preset plugin list fully intact and only extends the persona suffix; the Agent Teams tools themselves come from the factory bundle and switch on automatically with teams mode.

dsh-switchman README · Maintenance notes：- After a DSH upgrade, if the factory preset plugin list changed, re-sync `cordis.patch.yml` from the new `presets/*.patch.yml` (keeping the doctrine suffix and the compaction arbitration — `auto: false` on the `compaction-basic` rows), then reinstall.
- Protocol lines (`[SWITCHMAN:LANG|POOLS|WATERMARK|TEAMS]`) are deliberately English and byte-stable — don't localize them.
- `npm pack --dry-run` should keep the audited 60-file / ~380 kB tarball shape (~1.26 MB unpacked). `docs/` stays out of the package (it is not in `package.json files`), while the 11 `README.*` translations are always shipped by npm.
- **Zero runtime dependencies — a hard invariant.** Host-plane packages (`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, cordis, …) are declared as `peerDependencies` only, and the running DSH satisfies them from its own copy. An ordinary `dependencies` entry is physically installed into the profile workspace (`<profile>/node_modules/…`), where it shadows the host's copy for every other profile-resident plugin — this is exactly what crashed the dshmarket plugin market while 1.7.0 carried schemastery as a dependency (two schemastery instances in one process; the
